Sizes: S under a session, M about one, L two or three, XL four or more, with L and XL split into session-sized parts. Next to each feature, one tile per part (about a session each), so a row's length shows the work. Updated 2026-11-20; the editor shows the same list under Help > Features.

Planning notes: longest chains, how the sizes were set, research

Longest chains

What has to come first to reach the big ones. The order inside each step is free.

  • The mech as a character file: Input map → Character files and the Characters tab → Attributes, effects and abilities → Visual effects → Jetpack and grapple → The mech as a character file
  • Goo swarm enemies: Input map → Character files and the Characters tab → Attributes, effects and abilities → Behaviour host → Spots and claims → Steering and perception → Brains → Goo swarm enemies
  • Screens and menus: Variables → Readouts → UI core → Screens and menus
  • Vehicles: Input map → Character files and the Characters tab → Ways of moving and switching rules → Vehicles
  • Destructible props: Input map → Character files and the Characters tab → Attributes, effects and abilities → Health, shields and death → Destructible props

Research behind the new areas

Idles, barks and interaction

Crowds look wrong when everyone plays the same idle: guides suggest 3–5 idle variations per character type and random offsets so footsteps don't sync. Fidgets (scratching, looking around) start after standing still a while. Head look-at is a cheap procedural layer, and hands reach handles with two-bone IK that blends in and out; holding is easy, the blend is the hard part.

NPC animation guide (MoCap Online) · One line of look-at IK (Ergastulum) · Roblox IKControl (doorknob example) · Hand IK blend weights (Unreal forum)

Driving

Arcade handling starts simple and adds mechanics until it feels right: steering limited by speed (curbs understeer), the handbrake locks the rear wheels to start a drift, clean drifts refill boost, boost is spent on the way out. Simulation adds weight transfer and counter-steering; Beverly's vehicles start arcade with those as settings.

Racing game approaches and trade-offs (Game Developer) · Need for Speed Heat handling model (EA) · Disney Speedstorm drift diary

Flying

Arcade flight keeps pitch, yaw and roll with automatic banking in turns, plus speed and lift limits. Manoeuvres become moves: aileron roll (a full roll), barrel roll (a roll with a pull, evasive), dive, loop, Immelmann (half loop and half roll: turn back, gain height), split-S (the reverse: turn back, gain speed), stall turn, boost.

Arcade-style airplane (Godot recipes) · How to Immelmann (World of Warplanes) · How to barrel roll (World of Warplanes) · How to split-S (World of Warplanes)

Moves and abilities

Platformers hide forgiveness in jumping: coyote time (jump just after leaving an edge) and jump buffering. Air dashes usually reset on landing. Dodges pair a short invulnerability with a step; parries are timed blocks. Shooters add slide, wall-run and mantle; stealth adds crouch tiers, lean, cover and hiding in shadow.

GDevelop advanced jump · Celeste and forgiveness · Defensive mechanics · Stealth game animation design

World sizes, terrain, caves

Positions are 32-bit, so worlds past about 10 km jitter; the fix is a floating origin or camera-relative maths. Heightfields can't make overhangs; games add caves with sculpted volumes (smooth add / subtract shapes turned into meshes) or hand-made pieces, and build dungeons from modular kits, often laid out by a generator. Rooms joined by portals hide what can't be seen indoors; they don't suit open ground. Beverly's terrain is described by curves and strokes, not height images.

Godot: double precision for large worlds · How terrain works (Unity) · Voxel Tools overview · Dungeon generator from a kit · Godot rooms and portals

Water

Oceans layer a few Gerstner waves: stable and easy to tune. Rivers are paths with width, depth and flow speed per point; foam drifts with the flow. Waterfalls are usually custom pieces with mist and ripple rings where they land. Buoyancy samples the water height and pushes things up with drag. In Unreal, water fought with world streaming, so Beverly's water belongs to streaming regions from the start.

GPU Gems: effective water simulation · Planet Coaster 2 water · Unreal water and World Partition

Look: post-processing, styles, wind

Bevy 0.20 already has depth of field, motion blur, bloom, chromatic aberration, vignette, lens distortion, colour grading, auto exposure, SSAO, screen-space reflections, volumetric fog, a physical sky, TAA / SMAA and GPU occlusion culling, so these are mostly editor work. Cel shading bands light into 2–5 steps; outlines are cheap shells (gaps on hard edges) or precise screen edge detection (costlier, noisier); games often mix them. One wind (direction, strength, gusts) feeds foliage sway in two layers, cloth, flags, particles and sails.

bevy_post_process · Toon outlines (Kodeco) · Cel shading · Vegetation that reacts to the environment · Zephyr wind shaders

Multiplayer

Shooters and most online games use an authoritative server: each player's own moves show at once and are corrected when the server answers. Rollback (every machine simulates and rewinds on a wrong guess) suits two-player fighting games and needs a deterministic game. Multiplayer touches characters, physics, scripting and saving, so if it's wanted it should be decided early, even if it's built late.

Authoritative servers, relays and peer-to-peer (Edgegap) · Rollback netcode explained · Unity network topologies

Space and level edges

Classic space games fly like aircraft; Newtonian flight keeps momentum, and Elite layers a switchable flight assist over it so ships stay controllable. For the edge of a level, games warn and count down (“return to the combat area”), push the player back, damage them in a hazard zone or wrap them around; developers report wrapping rarely feels good in 3D and round areas beat square ones.

Elite Dangerous flight model · Star Citizen flight model (PC Gamer) · Border Patrol (TV Tropes) · Solutions for screen wrap (Sins forum)

Risks found in the second pass

Bevy releases every 3–4 months and each library has to catch up before Beverly can move, so Beverly stays pinned and upgrades on purpose (about a session each time). Physics: one collision world, not two. Animation: Prism has no skeletons yet, so pose and key comes to Beverly. Multiplayer: a fixed time step from the start. Effects: one particle system, Last Ascent's, and the Plume Editor's files as the effect format. Rasters: decals, reflections, foliage and terrain paint are kept as math, strokes or captured at load.

lightyear (prediction, rollback, Avian) · bevy-tnua · Bevy release process

Lighting: newer techniques (2026-11-20)

Bevy 0.20's Solari path tracer needs ray queries and now makes ReSTIR optional (off by default); wgpu's ray tracing is experimental with ray queries only, so vendor cluster acceleration structures (RTX Mega Geometry) aren't reachable yet. Unreal's virtual shadow maps keep static pages cached and redraw pages that moving things touch; MegaLights traces a fixed number of rays per pixel toward the important lights instead of a shadow map per light. For a no-ray-tracing tier: Unity's Surface Cache GI (shown in its Atrio demo) falls back to compute, AMD's Brixelizer GI is compute only, Lumen's software path uses cards and distance fields. Second-hand in places; primary pages were out of reach of the research session.

Bevy 0.20 release · Solari in Bevy 0.19 · wgpu ray tracing · RTX Mega Geometry (Vulkan samples) · Virtual shadow maps in Fortnite · MegaLights (Epic) · ReSTIR paper · Unity Surface Cache GI preview · AMD Brixelizer GI (GDC 2024) · Split Radiance Cascades

Building, vehicles, riding and many genres (2026-11-20)

Snap points (Valheim, Subnautica, KSP's attachment nodes with symmetry), live validity feedback (Valheim's support colours, Fortnite's red tiles), structure strength spreading from the ground, assemblies with joints that need to be strong, interiors that move with a body (Subnautica's Cyclops clipped the walker), control handover for vehicles and mounts (Unreal's unpossess, attach, possess; the rider-and-mount case needs two control paths), crowds with separate levels of detail for drawing, thinking and networking (Unreal's Mass), RTS orders as per-unit command queues and fog of war as a three-state grid, voxel games saving only edited chunks. Fortnite's devices (no-code placeable objects with options and events, code as the fallback) and Lyra's game features (genres as plugin bundles) are the model for modules and game packs. Most sources are guides and forums, not developer documentation.

Valheim building guide · KSP manual · Fortnite devices · Lyra sample game · Mass gameplay overview · RTS command queues and fog of war · Lockstep and determinism · Subnautica Cyclops interior bug · Vehicle enter and exit in Unreal · Voxel terrain overview

Custom shaders

L

Shaders as project assets (assets/shaders/*.wesl) with their settings shown as sliders, hot reload, errors in the island, and any material able to use one; raster hooks for moving vertices and cut-out edges.

ready · Engine budgets · on the Last Ascent path · needs Textures and materials ✓

Part 1 built 2026-11-19 (shader assets): shader.rs. A shader is assets/shaders/NAME.wesl, a fragment shader for Bevy's standard material with header comment lines (@setting name "Label" 0..5 = 1 / colour / toggle, @see-through, @raster vertex_offset / alpha_mask) that Beverly turns into setting_NAME() functions (added after the code) and a values uniform; a material file gets shader and shader_values; the extension picks its fragment shader per material (specialize), so any shader works, not a fixed set. The file is read again about twice a second (hot reload); a header that doesn't parse keeps the last good shader and says which line in the island. Materials tab: a Shader choice and its settings as rows; Assets lists Shaders; MCP: get_shader, write_shader, change_material takes shader and shader_values, list_assets has shaders. Test project tests/shaders. Part 2 built 2026-11-19 (errors and raster hooks): code the graphics card refuses reaches the island and get_shader's problem with its line (the render side reads the pipeline cache), and a failing shader fails a scripted test; @raster vertex_offset / alpha_mask are functions the shader defines (vertex_offset(world, normal, uv), alpha_mask(world, uv)) that Beverly runs in its own vertex stage and in the depth and shadow passes, so shadows follow, with the part's bounds grown by the declared reach; @see-through makes an opaque material blend and alpha_mask makes it cut out; a shader with hooks keeps its fragment under @if(!PREPASS_PIPELINE) (tests/shaders lean.wesl). Not skinned, no motion vectors or deferred. Still to do: the paint layers moving onto it (they are already a Beverly shader; the move is for virtual geometry part 3, where the strokes have to be worked out in the material pass), and virtual geometry's use of the hooks. Planned 2026-11-18 (user: many shaders will be written, mostly through Claude; the pipeline must take any shader, not a fixed set). Every material goes through it, so virtual geometry can bin clusters by raster shader the way Nanite's programmable raster does.

34.1 · a sessionShader assets: a settings header turned into sliders, hot reload, errors with the line, assigning a shader to a material; the paint layers move onto it

Stress level and memory meter

S

A dense generated level (many parts, lights, props and agents) and video memory in the performance meter.

ready · Engine budgets · on the Last Ascent path · needs Editor stats ✓ · Instancing and Unique ✓ · Lights, sun and sky ✓

Starts as the separate beverly-bench program (a download of its own, runs unattended at 1080p and 4K, writes a short plain-text log the user sends back: card report, polygons, lights with and without shadows, the moving-headlight case, agents on the processor, memory; no personal data). Bench built 2026-11-20 (`beverly-bench.exe`, code in editor/src/bench.rs and bench/{scenes,agents}.rs; the Windows build makes Beverly-bench-windows.zip beside the main zip): it draws into 1080p and 4K images and steps each series up (1 to 64 million triangles; 100 to 1,600 lights; 1 to 32 shadowed point lights; 1 to 8 moving shadowed headlights in a lit town of 300 lights and 600 props; 1 to 16 GB of textures; 1,000 to 1,000,000 agents on one core and on all), about four seconds a step, a series stopping when it runs under 20 fps; it writes beverly-bench-log.txt line by line (so a crash leaves what came before) with fps, worst 1%, the card's time, triangles, memory and a summary of the heaviest step that held 60 and 30 fps; --quick runs only the lightest steps. First log from the user's RTX 3050 (2026-11-20) showed the first version ran ahead of the card: frames queued up, so the frame rates were the processor's (63 million triangles read 153 fps while the card's own timer said 21 ms), memory grew to 22 GB and it crashed at 4K with 400 lights; the first scene was also wrongly stopped. Fixed the same day: each frame now waits for the card, the crowd test runs on a thread of its own after the card scenes, and a scene gets two minutes to get going. Waiting on a second log from the user's card (its results, such as 1,600 lights without shadows costing 17 ms of card time, and 8 moving shadowed headlights costing about 7.5 ms, are the first real numbers). The stress level builds from the same scene functions. Its scenes then become this level. Reference card: the user's own, 8 GB of video memory (user, 2026-11-20).

Runtime edits layer

M

Everything that changes while playing (player-built pieces, dug terrain, destroyed props, parts that moved, what a level looked like when you left) is a saved list of edits over the authored level; test mode throws it away, saves and level changes keep it.

ready · Editor foundations · on the Last Ascent path · needs The .bev file extension ✓ · Change tracking and undo as diffs ✓

Found in the 2026-11-20 review of the built code against the roadmap (docs/architecture.md). Voxel and survival games save only the edited chunks over a generated or authored world. One mechanism serves the save system, test-snapshot, returning to a level, building, digging and destruction. Digging stores shapes added or taken away (small and readable), and chunked data is allowed where it is clearly better (the no-raster rule is a guideline for game data).

39.1 · a sessionIn one go
40

Cached shadows

M

Cached shadow maps in two layers: the shadows of what never moves are drawn once and kept, only moving things are drawn each frame on top; shadow resolution by screen size.

ready · Engine budgets · on the Last Ascent path · needs Lights, sun and sky ✓ · Editor stats ✓

Design 2026-11-20 (the moving-headlight case): a moving shadowed light can't be cached, and each cached lamp a car passes would otherwise redraw the whole street, so the static layer is kept and only the car is redrawn into each lamp it passes. Lessons from Unreal's virtual shadow maps: changing a mesh's level of detail or streaming in detail does not invalidate pages by itself (do it ourselves), animated characters always count as moving, and skipping updates near the camera shows as artifacts. Headlights: a short shadow range inside a longer light range, shadows only for the nearest cars, a smaller shadow map. Costs by kind (estimates, unmeasured): unshadowed lights are cheap (hundreds); a shadowed point light draws the scene six times; the sun's cascades are a fixed cost.

Several levels and level exits

L

More than one level per project, with one named action, Go to level, that wires, triggers, the timeline, quests, screens and modules can all call.

planned · Logic and modules · on the Last Ascent path · needs Wires, buttons and moving parts ✓ · The .bev file extension ✓ · Runtime edits layer

Decided with the user 2026-11-20: a returning player finds their changes by default; the default transition is a fade with a loading screen. Anything that outputs a finished event can ask for a transition (a cutscene ending, a boss defeated, a quest complete, a death, a menu button, a module). Last Ascent leaves the outside level when entering the ship, replaced by a backdrop, then plays a cinematic from the escape ship while level two loads behind it. 77

Bezier pen tool

L

Click for corners, drag for smooth curves, close a loop on the first point; curves hug the surface under them and stay editable. Lays a strip, fills a shape, scatters along or inside it, or raises and carves.

ready · World building · on the Last Ascent path · needs Brush tool ✓

Part 1 built 2026-11-19 (the pen): P in the Level tab; click for a corner, drag for a smooth point, click the first point to close, Enter finishes; then drag points and handles, click the line to put a point on it, Alt + click a point (or Delete over it) removes it, Delete elsewhere removes the curve, click another curve to edit it, Alt while dragging breaks a handle; points snap to the grid like parts do and land on whatever surface is under the pointer. Curves live in the level file (curves: id, name, points with handle offsets, closed), one undo step per change; the code is curve.rs (the Bezier maths, tested) and editor/pen.rs. MCP: draw_shape (points as [x, y, z] or {at, handle_in, handle_out}, closed, shape to redraw, delete) and list_shapes (tests/mcp/check.py). Part 2, first slice built 2026-11-19 (stretches): each point carries how the line leaving it treats geometry, Ground (default), Over everything, Air or Fall, and the line seen is laid on what it meets (curve.rs laid, pen.rs surface; cached and relaid when the curve or any part changes): Ground takes the walkable surface (a top face, or a part tagged Ground or Water; never one tagged Paths ignore or an invisible collider) within half a metre up or two down from where it was, so it lies on a slab, passes under a prop or ceiling and bridges gaps; Over takes anything visible within 1.5 m up; Air ignores geometry; Fall leaves along its handle and ends where it lands. Ground stretches draw solid, Air and Fall dashed; a small button by the selected point switches its stretch (a new point goes on as the last one went); the Ground and Paths ignore tags are new surface tags; draw_shape points take stretch and list_shapes says it. Strips built 2026-11-19: the pen has a panel (Inspect while it is out: the curve's name, Paint a strip with a material, Width, Edge, Strength); a strip paints the laid line as brush strokes onto the part under each step of it (the part whose top face the point is on, so a prop the line passes through isn't painted and a stretch in the air paints nothing), kept in step with the curve: the strokes are the parts' own, marked with the curve (Stroke.curve), made again in place when the curve, its strip or the geometry changes and taken away with the strip or curve, in the same undo step; draw_shape takes strip {material, width, edge, strength} (null removes it) and list_shapes says it. Fills built 2026-11-19: the pen's panel has a Fill group (Fill the inside, the material it paints, Feather, Strength); a fill paints the ground inside the curve (an open curve is closed by a straight line), the paint shader working out the inside and the feathered edge from the curve's outline, so nothing is painted into an image; it goes to each part with walkable ground inside the outline (a top face within a step of the line's height, as a Ground path counts it), not to props standing on that ground or parts tagged Paths ignore, and lies under a strip on the same curve; like strips its strokes are the parts' own (Stroke.fill, with the outline in the part's own frame like a brush stroke's), made again in place when the curve, its fill or the geometry changes and in the same undo step; draw_shape takes fill {material, feather, strength} (null removes it) and list_shapes says it. Still to do: the path-wide default and Sag for air, the slope limit, scatter, and picking a curve without the pen; height along curves waits for terrain (user, 2026-11-19). Scatter, as the user describes it (2026-11-19): bits of random, context-appropriate debris that make a level feel varied and detailed (in a nature scene tree stumps, logs, boulders, sticks, brambles), so it places items picked at random from a set the user chooses, along or inside a curve. Decided with the user 2026-11-19: a path has two modes, Ground only (default: drapes onto the ground and ignores props, scatter and other paths) and Over everything (follows any geometry it meets); the surface each point was clicked on decides which level it follows, the path stays on that level between points, ground means surfaces within a slope limit and objects below step height, gaps are bridged, Water counts as ground; where two ground paths cross, the later one wins (order keys Ctrl+[ and ], Ctrl+Shift for ends, with a list in the Inspect panel, see the order note on the brush). Refined 2026-11-19 (user: a path crosses many surfaces; tags as well as rules; scatter on the ground, deep select for manual adjustment): the mode is per stretch (stored on a point, for the segment leaving it) with a path-wide default: Ground (walkable surfaces: ground, road, steps, interior floor; the path takes the walkable surface nearest in height to the previous sample within the step height, starting from the clicked level; ceilings and invisible colliders never count), Over everything, Air (ignores geometry; Sag for a rope) and Fall (leaves along its handle and drops until it hits a surface; a faucet stream is Fall then Ground). Tags: Ground forces a part to count, Paths ignore forces it out, Water counts. Precedence: the stretch's own behaviour, tags, the path's default, the slope and step rules. Scatter sits on the surface the path is following and never on other scatter; deep select (gesture to choose: Ctrl+click or double-click in; Alt is taken by the pen and brush) picks one scatter instance to nudge, delete or detach, kept as overrides by position along the curve (they can drift if the curve is reshaped a lot; Turn into items freezes everything). Confirmed by the user 2026-11-19: ground stretches draw as a solid line and air stretches dashed, with a small button on the selected point to switch its stretch behaviour; deep select is a double-click into the shape. Planned 2026-11-17. The one curve tool: the Paths tool draws its rails, patrols and roads with it. Stored as control points and handles. MCP: draw_shape (points, handles, closed, layer, width, feather). Idea (user, 2026-11-17): terrain features drawn with the pen, such as cliffs: a wedge along the curve with strong variation, and scatter (rocks) masking its seams. Live curves plus Turn into items (user, 2026-11-17). Characters tab later: hair, cloth strips and jewellery drawn with the pen, moving with physics. Keys (2026-11-17): P is the pen in the Level tab; points can also go in the air for camera and flying paths (the Paths overlay). Review 2026-11-20 found the fill outline stored in world coordinates (it would break on a moving part or after a region or origin shift); fixed 2026-11-20: the outline is stored in the part's own frame and the shader tests inside in that frame (test: a fill stays on a part that is moved and turned). Scatter is its own entry now.

Planned 2026-11-21 with the user: tag a group 'collider' or 'breakable', or a material 'stone', and Beverly sets it up, with overrides. 'collider' means an invisible collision shape for the group it sits in (the Unreal and Godot convention); if a model has any, only colliders collide (models collide as drawn otherwise, so the drawn-and-solid meaning needs no word). The GLB contract both programs follow is docs/prism-glb.md, an addendum to Prism's brief 50 sent to the Prism session: roles as a list on groups and components (extras.prism.roles), the instance's Prism tag (extras.prism.tag), a material's Surface (material extras.prism.surface). Waits its turn in the build order (user). From the Gates of Heaven design (docs/games/gates-of-heaven.md, 2026-11-22): the word node (a small cube named Node) is an attachment node: the cube's centre and axes give its position and facing, and the cube isn't drawn.

Terrain from curves and strokes

XL

Terrain described as control points, curves and stroke operations (raise along a curve, flatten a pad, carve a bed, noise layers), drawn straight from that description on the GPU: no stored meshes and no height images.

planned · World building · on the Last Ascent path · needs World settings · Bezier pen tool · Brush tool ✓

Height images from other tools could be converted into strokes later, if wanted. Collision (user, 2026-11-15: no meshes where a height function does it cheaper): the ground is the height function itself as a custom shape in Avian that answers rays exactly (standing on it: the walker's tnua sensor as a ray instead of a disc; feet and foot placement, grapple, camera, bullets, placing things), plus a small contact rule of Beverly's own, since Parry works out contact between solid shapes only for its built-in ones: each step, loose bodies' lowest points are checked against the height and pushed up and out along the slope, and ground steeper than a set limit (banks taller than the walker's 0.45 m step) pushes characters back like a wall. Check: sampled points agree with the height function, the walker climbs stairs and is stopped by a steep bank, a loose crate settles on a slope. Its stroke tools are the brush; its curve tools the pen (user, 2026-11-17). Needs the pen, not the Paths tool (2026-11-17): the pen is the one curve tool, and Paths adds the timeline overlay terrain doesn't use. Ground without meshes (user, 2026-11-17: not a fan of meshes for world ground; tessellation can be built if needed): the ground is drawn from its description each frame, the way the grass carpet draws blades.

Research 2026-11-20 (second-hand, to confirm from primary sources): Unity's Surface Cache GI (shown in its Atrio demo) uses hardware ray tracing where there is any and a compute fallback where not; AMD's Brixelizer GI is compute only on sparse distance fields; Lumen's software path uses cards and distance-field tracing; Split Radiance Cascades (2026 paper) stores probes in a sparse hash near visible surfaces. Beverly's parts are mostly primitives, so cards and distance fields are cheap to make. Nothing ready-made exists for Bevy: Solari needs ray queries.

The mech as a character file

L

Last Ascent's mech rebuilt from Beverly's blocks; the extra Last Ascent editor and player retire.

planned · Characters and movement · on the Last Ascent path · needs Joint chains and procedural animation · Attributes, effects and abilities · Visual effects · Character camera and controls · Jetpack and grapple · HUD editor · Physics for loose objects ✓ · Ways of moving and switching rules

Scripted tests record today's mech before anything changes, so the port can be compared step by step. What to look for when converting it (Physics part 2, 2026-11-15): Beverly no longer hands a game's character the level's triangles (Play::world, with pieces() and offsets(), is gone), so Last Ascent's own editor and player stop building once they update past this; the user chose to rebuild the mech after Beverly is built, not to port it twice. Collision is now Avian's world while playing (physics.rs): each Solid part is a body tagged PartBody(id), still ones static, Moves ones kinematic (their LinearVelocity carries what stands on them), Loose ones dynamic, plus the ground at y = 0. The mech's own physics maps onto it: its sphere-against-triangles step becomes a body of its own (a bevy_tnua character like the walker in play.rs, or Avian's MoveAndSlide), its raycast (grapple, camera, ground) Avian's SpatialQuery::cast_ray, its ground_y (the legs' foot placement) a ray down, and riding moving parts comes free. Physics runs on the fixed 60 Hz step (single precision, Avian's Gravity 9.81 with GravityScale for heavier falls): the mech's movement moves from Update with a variable step to FixedUpdate, catching one-off keys every frame as play.rs does (Play::press), and still sets Play::feet for buttons. Its recorded runs (walk, jets, grapple) will drift with the new collision: compare them, and re-record only when the user agrees.
